description: Gold standard validation of keyword-based non-Western framework scoring

nw_confucian.primary_fp_pattern: Chinese NLP benchmarks (ACLUE, C3Bench, AncientBench, etc.) trigger on 'Chinese' keywords without Confucian philosophical content

nw_ubuntu.primary_fp_pattern: Ubuntu Linux OS references; passing mentions without philosophical engagement

nw_islamic_ethics.primary_fp_pattern: Arabic/Persian NLP benchmarks where Islamic content is one test category, not substantive ethical analysis

nw_buddhist.primary_fp_pattern: Buddhist text corpora for NLP (not ethics); religion-as-test-subject bias studies; Thai/Buddhist cultural benchmarks

nw_dharmic.primary_fp_pattern: NLP on Hindu/Vedic texts (sentiment analysis, topic modeling) conflated with dharmic ethical analysis

nw_indigenous_relational.primary_fp_pattern: NLP/language tech mentioning 'indigenous' languages without engaging Indigenous ethical frameworks

nw_buen_vivir.primary_fp_pattern: Passing mentions of buen vivir in papers primarily about other frameworks

key_finding: The keyword scorer achieves near-perfect recall (0.995 mean) but low precision (0.358 mean). The dominant FP pattern across all frameworks is NLP benchmarks and text corpora that MENTION a tradition's language/texts without ENGAGING its ethical framework. Islamic ethics has the highest precision (0.706) because its keywords are more specific to ethical concepts (maqasid, fiqh, fatwa). Confucian, Buddhist, Dharmic, and Buen Vivir have the lowest precision (0.16-0.20) due to cultural/linguistic keyword overlap.
recommendation: The paper should report both raw detected counts and precision-adjusted estimates. For example, Confucian raw=86, precision-adjusted≈14. This changes the narrative: genuine philosophical engagement with non-Western frameworks is even rarer than the raw counts suggest.
